stem: Which list of wait times has the smallest standard deviation?
stimulus: A county health department recorded how long, in minutes, patients waited to be seen at four walk-in clinics. Each list below gives one clinic's wait times for five weekday mornings.
explanation: Standard deviation tells you how far the values usually sit from their mean. In 18, 19, 20, 21, 22, no value is more than 2 minutes from the mean of 20. Every other list has values that are farther from its own mean, so this one has the smallest standard deviation.

A.why: You went by how few different values the list has. It only has three, but four of its five values are 10 minutes from the mean of 20, so it is widely spread.

C.why: This list is the most spread out. Its values go as far as 16 minutes from the mean, so it has the largest standard deviation, not the smallest.

D.why: You picked the list with the smallest numbers. Small values do not mean small spread. These values sit up to 4 minutes from their mean of 6, which is more than the 2 minutes in 18, 19, 20, 21, 22.

stem: Which statement correctly compares the means and the standard deviations of the sodium contents of the two brands?
stimulus:
A nutrition lab measured the sodium content, in milligrams, of five servings of each of two brands of canned soup.
Sodium Content per Serving (milligrams)
Brand | Serving 1 | Serving 2 | Serving 3 | Serving 4 | Serving 5
Brand P | 320 | 300 | 360 | 340 | 380
Brand Q | 520 | 500 | 560 | 540 | 580
choices: The means are equal, and the standard deviations are equal.
The means are different, and the standard deviations are different.
The means are different, and the standard deviations are equal.
The means are equal, and the standard deviations are different.
explanation: Each Brand Q serving has exactly 200 mg more sodium than the matching Brand P serving. Adding the same amount to every value moves the center from 340 mg to 540 mg, so the means are different. The values sit the same distances from their own mean, so the standard deviations are equal.

A.why: You saw that the spread is the same but missed that every Brand Q value is 200 mg higher. That shift makes the means different.

B.why: You treated a change in location as a change in spread. Moving the whole set up by 200 mg changes the mean but not the standard deviation.

D.why: You swapped the two measures. The mean is the one that changes and the standard deviation is the one that stays the same, not the other way around.

stem: Which statement correctly compares the two groups?
stimulus:
Immunologists tested two vaccine formulations, each given to 20 volunteers. For each volunteer, they recorded the number of days after the shot until a measurable antibody response appeared.
Days Until Antibody Response
Days | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7
Group A (number of volunteers) | 1 | 2 | 14 | 2 | 1
Group B (number of volunteers) | 6 | 3 | 2 | 3 | 6
choices: The means are equal, and the standard deviations are equal.
The means are equal, and group A's standard deviation is larger.
Group A's mean is larger, and group A's standard deviation is smaller.
The means are equal, and group A's standard deviation is smaller.
explanation: Both groups are symmetric around 5 days, so both means are 5. In group A, 14 of the 20 volunteers are at exactly 5 days. In group B, 12 of the 20 are at 3 or 7 days, as far from the center as possible. Group A is more tightly clustered, so its standard deviation is smaller.

A.why: You judged spread by the range. Both groups run from 3 to 7 days, but group B has far more volunteers at the extremes, so its standard deviation is larger.

B.why: You reversed the comparison. Group A is the one bunched at the center, so its standard deviation is the smaller one.

C.why: You read the frequency 14 as if it were a number of days. Group A's mean is 5 days, the same as group B's.

stem: For which city do the daily high temperatures have the largest standard deviation?
stimulus:
A meteorology student recorded the daily high temperature, in degrees Fahrenheit, in four cities over the same five days.
Daily High Temperature (°F)
City | Mon | Tue | Wed | Thu | Fri
Ashford | 63 | 61 | 65 | 69 | 67
Brinley | 65 | 50 | 65 | 80 | 65
Corwen | 50 | 80 | 65 | 50 | 80
Dunmore | 82 | 80 | 84 | 88 | 86
choices: Ashford
Brinley
Corwen
Dunmore
explanation: Brinley and Corwen both have a mean of 65°F and both run from 50°F to 80°F. But four of Corwen's five highs are 15 degrees from the mean, while three of Brinley's are exactly at the mean. Corwen's values are the farthest from center overall, so its standard deviation is the largest.

A.why: Ashford's highs are all within 4 degrees of their mean. That gives one of the smallest standard deviations, not the largest.

B.why: You judged spread by the range. Brinley and Corwen have the same range, but most of Brinley's highs sit right at the mean, so its standard deviation is smaller.

D.why: You picked the city with the highest temperatures. Dunmore's values are just Ashford's pattern moved up, so its spread is small even though its center is high.

stem: Which statement correctly compares the standard deviations of the two lists?
stimulus:
A folklorist counted the number of distinct story motifs in six recorded versions of the same folktale from each of two regions.
Region 1: 8, 9, 10, 10, 11, 12
Region 2: 4, 6, 10, 10, 14, 16
choices: The standard deviation of the Region 1 counts is greater than that of the Region 2 counts.
The standard deviation of the Region 1 counts is less than that of the Region 2 counts.
The standard deviation of the Region 1 counts is equal to that of the Region 2 counts.
The standard deviation of the Region 1 counts is exactly 8 less than that of the Region 2 counts.
explanation: Both lists have a mean of 10. Region 1's counts are no more than 2 from 10, while Region 2's counts reach 6 away. Region 1 is clustered more tightly, so its standard deviation is less.

A.why: You reversed the comparison. Region 2's counts are the ones farther from the mean, so Region 2 has the greater standard deviation.

C.why: The lists have the same mean, the same median, and the same number of distinct values, but none of those measures spread. Region 2's values are much farther from 10.

D.why: 8 is the difference between the ranges (12 minus 4), not between the standard deviations. Range and standard deviation are different measures, and the real difference here is about 3.

stem: Which list of heart rates has the largest standard deviation?
stimulus: A sports scientist measured the heart rates, in beats per minute, of six athletes one minute after each of four training drills. Each list below gives the results for one drill.
explanation: In the first list, every heart rate is 10 beats per minute from the mean of 150. None of the values is close to the center, so this list has the most spread and the largest standard deviation.

B.why: You judged spread by the range. This list stretches from 135 to 165, but four of its six values are within 1 of the mean, so its typical distance from center is smaller.

C.why: This list is clustered within 3 of its mean of 150. That makes it one of the smallest standard deviations, not the largest.

D.why: You picked the list with the highest heart rates. A higher center does not mean more spread, and these values are within 3 of their mean.

Lyle's is greater, since more of its samples are far from 20.

They are equal, since both sets have a mean of 20.

A.why: You mixed up the two rows. Marsh's samples are the ones piled up at 20. Lyle's are the ones pushed out to 18 and 22.

C.why: You judged spread by the range alone. Both sets run from 18 to 22, but Lyle has many more samples at those extremes.

stem: Which statement correctly compares the standard deviations of the crab lengths at the two pools?
stimulus:
A marine biologist measured the carapace lengths, in millimeters, of seven juvenile crabs from each of two tide pools.
Pool P: 30, 40, 40, 40, 40, 40, 50
Pool Q: 31, 31, 31, 40, 49, 49, 49
choices: Pool P's is greater, since its lengths have the larger range.
They are equal, since both pools have a mean length of 40 mm.
Pool P's is greater, since it has more lengths equal to 40 mm.
Pool P's is less, since most of its lengths equal the mean.
explanation: Both pools have a mean of 40 mm. Five of Pool P's seven lengths are exactly 40 mm, while six of Pool Q's are 9 mm from 40. Pool P's data are bunched at the center, so its standard deviation is less, even though its range is slightly larger.

A.why: You judged spread by the range alone. Pool P's range (20 mm) is larger, but only two of its values are away from the mean, while almost all of Pool Q's are.

B.why: Having the same mean does not make the spreads the same. You also need to look at how far the values sit from 40 mm, and Pool Q's sit much farther.

C.why: You reversed what clustering means. Values piled up at the mean make the standard deviation smaller, not larger.

stem: Which of the following statements correctly compares the standard deviations of the two data sets?
stimulus:
A nutrition researcher recorded the daily fiber intake, in grams, of 7 participants in each of two groups.

Group A: 10, 14, 15, 15, 15, 16, 20
Group B: 10, 11, 12, 15, 18, 19, 20
choices: The standard deviation of Group A is less than that of Group B.
The standard deviation of Group A is greater than that of Group B.
The standard deviations of Group A and Group B are equal.
There is not enough information to compare the standard deviations.
explanation: Both groups have a mean of 15 g. In Group A, five of the seven values are within 1 g of 15, and only 10 and 20 are far away. In Group B, only one value sits at 15 and the rest are 3 to 5 g away. Group A is bunched more tightly around the center, so its standard deviation is smaller.

B.why: You saw that Group A has a clear cluster and Group B doesn't, but you reversed the conclusion. Values clustered near the mean give a smaller standard deviation, not a larger one.

C.why: You judged spread by the range. Both groups run from 10 to 20 and share a mean of 15, but range only looks at the two endpoints. Standard deviation depends on how far every value is from the mean, and Group B has more values far from 15.

D.why: You assumed you would need to calculate the standard deviations. You have every data value, and that is enough to compare how far each group sits from its mean without any calculation.

stem: Which of the following statements correctly compares the standard deviations of the jump heights for the two teams?
stimulus:
A sports scientist measured the vertical jump heights of five athletes on each of two teams.

Vertical Jump Height (centimeters)
Team | Athlete 1 | Athlete 2 | Athlete 3 | Athlete 4 | Athlete 5
Team X | 40 | 42 | 44 | 46 | 48
Team Y | 50 | 52 | 54 | 56 | 58
choices: The standard deviation for Team X is less than that for Team Y.
The standard deviation for Team X is greater than that for Team Y.
The standard deviations for Team X and Team Y are equal.
There is not enough information to compare the standard deviations.
explanation: Each Team Y height is exactly 10 cm more than the matching Team X height. Adding the same amount to every value moves the mean up by 10 but doesn't change how far any value is from the mean. The spread is identical, so the standard deviations are equal.

A.why: You compared the centers instead of the spreads. Team Y's heights are larger, which means a larger mean. It doesn't mean a larger standard deviation, since the values are spaced exactly as they are for Team X.

B.why: You decided the shift changed the spread and then picked Team X as more spread out. A shift of 10 cm changes neither team's distances from its own mean, so neither standard deviation is larger.

D.why: You assumed you would need to calculate each standard deviation. The table gives every value, and the matching pattern of gaps (every 2 cm) is enough to show the spreads are the same.
